firstMessage.rawMarkdown:
The core of ARC-AGI is to test and facilitate the development of efficient skill
acquisition in AI, which François Chollet believes is the core of intelligence.

Now GPT-6 reaches a basically perfect score in ARC-AGI-3 (99.9%), double the human average. It's even found to be more "efficient" than humans — requiring fewer attempts than most people before solving a problem.

But how should we interpret this? Many people just judge based on an overall final score, which I don't think is informative. Have you looked at the details in how LLMs approach ARC-AGI-3? Have you observed or built in "efficient skill acquisition" capabilities?
